newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Sierra Leone rebels say truce violated.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone rebels say truce violated.

text.p: Sierra Leone rebels said on Friday government forces were violating the accord they signed last November 30 on ending their country's six-year civil war.
Revolutionary United Front (RUF) spokesman Alieu Mustapha said camps where RUF guerrillas had assembled since the signing of the Abidjan pact had been attacked in Kailahun district.

"On 14th January 1997, Godama, Glayala and Jaama were attacked. On the 15th January 1997, Kpolu and Mende Buima were attacked and some of these towns are still occupied by government forces," he said in a statement.

"RUF views this as a lack of commitment on the part of the government and as ploy to provoke the RUF into launching a counter-offensive, something we have patiently refused to do," added the statement issued in Abidjan, Ivory Coast, where the RUF leadership is based.
The statement was released ahead of a meeting of the U.N. Security Council early next week to discuss the sending of neutral monitors to observe the ceasefire.

In a letter to United Nations Secretary General Kofi Annan issued along with the statement, RUF leader Foday Sanko said Sierra Leone did not need a classic peacekeeping force with all the cost involved.

"We believe the Abidjan Peace Accord is very clear about a Neutral Monitoring Group and not a peacekeeping force. We want to have the country demilitarised as much as possible," Sankoh said in the January 13 letter.
He said RUF had full control over its fighters and would present no security problem and called on the government to control the army and its militia allies known as Kamajos.
There was no immediate comment from the government or the military on RUF's charges of ceasefire violations.
But President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah's senior adviser, Sheka Mansaray, acknowledged security problems from other armed elements who were not party to the peace accord.
He blamed some attacks on people desperate for food.
"Apart from RUF combatants even other people who are short of food will carry out attacks for food," Mansaray said. "So the government is also trying to help these distressd people."
